baseline.name: Indexed interleave into output
baseline.approach: Write nums[i] to output[2*i] and nums[n+i] to output[2*i+1].
baseline.space: O(1) auxiliary state plus O(n) output

archived.name: Pointer-cursor interleave
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary pointers plus O(n) output

why: The pointer version expresses the same two reads and two writes per pair as the indexed baseline.
quantitative_comparison: Both read and write exactly 2n elements. Pointer syntax does not establish fewer compiled instructions or lower runtime; no advantage is measured.
tradeoffs: Requires numsSize==2*n, valid lengths and successful output allocation. Readability preferences and compiler optimization determine any constant-level differences.
evidence_basis: Static equivalence of data movement in the two formulations; no generated-code or timing study.
